title: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review - notes
content:
Weekly ops sync / reliability review - prep notes (meeting 2026-03-03)

Attendees: Ethan, Ravi, Claire, Maya (notes) + optional: product on call (Anita)
Duration: 45m

High level goals for this sync:
- Quick SLO health check & identify anything requiring immediate mitigation
- Paging trends and on-call burden review (PD noise)
- Review top 2 incidents from last week and action item status
- Decide follow-ups to move to incubation/epics or runbook updates

Draft agenda:
1) Quick metrics snapshot (5m)
   - Service SLOs (prod):
   * API generation latency SLO (p99 < 400ms) - current week p99 = 410ms (missed ~0.9% of requests)
   * Error rate SLO (5xx) target <0.1% - current = 0.18% (0.08% burn this week)
   * Embeddings pipeline availability >99.95% - current = 99.96% (on target)
   - Error budget burn: cumulative ~7% for Feb -> still healthy but trending up (DB connection spikes)

2) Paging trends & PD noise (10m)
   - Total pages last 7 days: 42 (up from 28 previous week)
   - Top sources: DB connection timeouts (14), tokenization OOM (7), autoscaler flaps (6)
   - On-call load: median pages per engineer/day = 0.9; top 10% saw 3+ pages/day
   - Notes: DB spike pattern aligns with nightly backup window + transient pool exhaustion; need mitigation (pooled connections + circuit breaker)

3) Incident deep dive #1 - INC-2026-02-25 (15m)
   - Summary: Production API error surge due to a backlog in the prediction-workers queue after model rollout + spike in request size; connection pool exhaustion to primary DB replica caused cascading 5xx
   - Impact: ~2h partial degradation for generation endpoints; customer retries increased cost of serving; error budget burn ~3.5% that window
   - Root cause (tentative): rollout increased average per-request CPU and kept DB connections open longer; autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough due to cooldown settings
   - Actions in flight: revert rollout -> done, adjust rollout canary rules -> PR open (infra#312), increase DB pool limit on read replicas (Ravi), add circuit breaker on worker side (Ethan)
   - Follow-ups: add load test for rollout scenarios (owner: Claire, due 2026-03-17), update rollout runbook to include DB pool checks (owner: Maya, due 2026-03-10)

4) Incident deep dive #2 - tokenization OOMs (10m)
   - Summary: tokenization service OOMs for large prompt batches after cache eviction; paging pattern shows memory growth preceding crash
   - Impact: intermittent latency spikes and tokenization failures; some downstream request failures retried and caused queueing
   - Actions: short-term: raise memory limit on tokenizers in prod pool (done), enable early rejection for >1MB prompts (PR pending), instrument mem growth metrics (Ethan)

5) Runbook and tooling items (3m)
   - PD escalation thresholds need tuning: too many low-severity pages fired during maintenance windows -> propose a maintenance-suppression mode for non-critical alerts (Ravi to prototype)
   - Add SLO dashboards per release channel (canary/stable) to spot rollout regressions earlier (Claire)

6) Action items and owners (2m)
   - Ravi: increase DB read replica pool, and document limits (due 2026-03-08)
   - Ethan: circuit breaker implementation + mem growth instrumentation (due 2026-03-12)
   - Claire: rollout load test, and SLO dashboard for canary (due 2026-03-17)
   - Maya: update rollout runbook + follow up on PR infra#312 (due 2026-03-10)
   - Team: review PD noise and propose suppression policy (sync by 2026-03-09)

Open questions / notes to follow up:
- Should we add DB pool saturation alarms tied to queue length to preempt cascade? (yes - propose threshold and owner)
- Can product limit max prompt size per plan to reduce risk of OOMs? Invite product on next sync
- Autoscaler cooldown seems too aggressive during sudden rollout traffic; consider reducing cooldown for critical services

Misc notes / personal TODOs:
- Capture meeting notes + paste into INC-2026-02-25 postmortem (Maya)
- Add runbook snippet for rollback criteria to Confluence (link: CONFT-ops-runbook)
- Remind infra to coordinate nightly backup timing with SRE for DB heavy windows

Quick links:
- Incident: INC-2026-02-25
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/312
- Runbook: CONFT-ops-runbook

-- end of prep notes
